evals.name: auto-loop-on-the-fixture
evals.setup: A git repository holding a copy of `web/evals/assets/` as its only commit, clean tree: a plain HTML, CSS, and JS device dashboard (`index.html`, `app.js`, `lib.js`, `style.css`) with a hash router — Devices (`#/devices`, the landing page, listing 2000 devices with a search box and a sort button), a device detail view (`#/device/<id>`), and Settings — under one shared header. `server.py`, a stdlib Python server with no live reload, serves the files and a JSON API and appends every request to `requests.log` (ignored by `.gitignore`). `package.json` declares no scripts and no dependencies. The `Makefile` has `serve` (`python3 server.py`, port 8138), `check` (`./check.sh`, green on this tree), and `bench` (runs `tests/*.bench.js` with the helper in `tests/bench.js`). `python3 server.py` is serving on port 8138, the only listening port. Chrome DevTools MCP is connected with a visible window; the craft plugin is installed; the app has no login; nothing forbids committing. The user answers the start message with `ok`.
evals.requires: A visible Chrome driven by Chrome DevTools MCP, the fixture's server on port 8138, Node.js, and the craft plugin. Without a browser no measurement is established; a run that cannot meet this reports the scenario blocked.
